newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-European stocks turn mixed, FTSE falls.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-European stocks turn mixed, FTSE falls.

text.p: European bourses were mixed on Friday afternoon, with London's FTSE-100 index falling back into negative ground from its record high set earlier in the session.

The dollar and mark steadied against the yen, with the mark recovering from a near 23-month low against the Japanese unit. Activity was quiet because U.S. markets are closed for the Independence Day holiday.

Gold prices tumbled below $325 per ounce to hit a 12-year low on fears of central bank liquidation, as bullion loses its "safe-haven" status against turbulence in the global economy and as a hedge against inflation.
Prices dropped sharply after the Reserve Bank of Australia said on Thursday it had sold 167 tonnes of gold from its reserves, reducing its holdings to 80 tonnes.
Many analysts and dealers now see gold sliding to $300 or lower.
"If central banks are prowling around, there's no given level at which gold will settle," an analyst said.
The FTSE-100 index was volatile, opening lower, climbing to a record high at 4,879 and then dropping into negative territory again.
Traders attributed the swings to derivatives-related activity.
"It is difficult to tell how much of today's business was genuine trading and how much related to arbitrage positions in the derivatives," said Tim Huddart, Merrill Lynch UK equities strategist.
Exporter stocks were London's biggest losers, suffering from worries the pound's recent strength would cut into profits. A strong currency makes exports less competitive in world markets.
Germany's DAX index closed sharply higher, but off its record 3,945.68 reached early in the day.
Traders said shares were boosted by Wall Street's strong close overnight.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average soared 100.43 points on Thursday to close at a record 7,895.81 after a smaller-than-expected rise in U.S. June payrolls confirmed moderating growth amid low inflation.
Munich Re's 485-mark jump to 5,400, after the company said overnight it would merge its Hamburg-Mannheimer AG unit with Victoria Holding AG VOLGn.D, also provided the DAX with a lift.
France's CAC-40 index was slightly lower, consolidating recent gains. But activity was sluggish due to the U.S. holiday.
In currency markets, sterling lingered just below its March 1991 high of 2.9665 against the mark, helped by perceptions the UK will raise interest rates at next week's monetary meeting.
The mark also weakened against the yen, falling to a near 23-month low, before steadying at slightly higher levels.

"The only thing that will help the mark right now is the complete collapse of EMU (economic and monetary union)," said Gerard Lyons, DKB chief economist. "Given that looks very unlikely, mark/yen is a one-way bet."
EMU is seen hurting the mark because the single currency planned to replace participants' national currencies is expected to be softer than Germany's currency now.

But the mark's weakness helped the dollar steady after the U.S. unit slipped on Thursday on the soft U.S. jobs report. The dollar fell on perceptions the Federal Reserve would not have to raise U.S. rates at its next policy-making meeting in August to rein in growth and inflation.
The dollar's softness had lingered into early European trading on Friday, hitting a one-week low against the yen. But the currency subsequently found support above 113 yen and 1.75 marks.
CURRENCIES AT 1435 GMT
The dollar was at 113.62 yen and 1.7522 marks comapred with 113.45 and 1.7495 in late Europe on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1435 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 30.3 points at 4,801.40.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 4.75 at 2,932.23.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended bourse trade up 55.14 at 3,942.53.
PRECIOUS METALS

London gold was fixed at $325.20 per ounce in the morning, the lowest since January 1996 and sharply lower than Thursday's close at $331.50. Silver opened lower at $4.57, down from $4.65 at Thursday's close
